In this example, the variable limit $x$ is located on the lower limit. To apply FTC II, we need the variable to be on the upper limit. Using the properties of definite integrals, we can write

$$
h(x)={\int }_{x}^{1}(2{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}t=-{\int }_{1}^{x}(2{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore, by FTC II, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}{\int }_{x}^{1}(2{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-{\int }_{1}^{x}(2{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\int }_{1}^{x}(2{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-(2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of ${h}^{′}(0),$ we substitute $x=0$ in the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(0) & =-(2\cdot {0}^{3}+{0}^{2}-1) \\  & =-(0+0-1) \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$
